newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Future HK lawmakers discourage balcony protest.
newsitem.headline: Future HK lawmakers discourage balcony protest.

text.p: Hong Kong's future Beijing-backed legislature said on Thursday it would allow ousted democratic lawmakers to enter the building briefly right after the British colony's reversion to China next week.
But it said a planned balcony protest against their removal would not be "appropriate".

The Beijing-appointed Provisional Legislative Council (PLC) said in a statement that plans by current Legislative Council members to use the balcony for a pro-democracy demonstration after the handover at midnight on Monday would set an unwanted precedent.

"Members of the PLC have agreed...that a flexible and sensible approach should be adopted to enable these outgoing legislators to enter the...building after midnight for a reasonable period of time," the statement said.
"As for the use of the balcony...for the delivery of manifestos,...PLC members believed it might not be an appropriate venue for such a purpose," it added.
"Over the last 100 years since the building is in use no such activity has been approved, (and) it is not the right time to set such a precedent now."
Despite furious complaints from London, the Provisional Legislative Council is to replace the democratically-elected Legislative Council when the territory reverts to China on July 1.
Outgoing lawmakers say they plan to read a proclamation from the balcony condemning their successors as undemocratic.
